title: safetyism
summary: The tacit ideology that the government’s main goal should be to minimize risks rather than balance them against benefits.
whyItMatters: The concept is useful because it names a governing style in which caution becomes the default answer even when tradeoffs are unavoidable. It often appears in debates about regulation, public health, speech, and education.
notes: Used carefully, the term points to a real tension between resilience and protection. Used lazily, it can flatten serious moral disagreements into a single accusation of overprotection.
